text:
Edmonton keeps winning, and Mathieu Joseph keeps getting less of it. The two-time Cup winner with Tampa Bay played 8.8 and 8.7 minutes in the last two games, and his ice time over the last ten is down 2.42 minutes a night from where it was. That fits the five-on-five picture: the Oilers have taken just 34% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, more than 17 points worse than when he sits. Sportskeeda listed him among the most disappointing Oilers after the 5-4 loss to Anaheim.

The eight points in 21 games look fine for a depth role, but they lean on luck. He has three goals on 1.82 expected and is shooting 16.7%, above even the top of our range for him (15.6%). His defensive case is last season's: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting fewer chances with him out there than against 86% of forwards, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 73% of his exits leaving with possession. That is the version his minutes depend on.
headline: Mathieu Joseph's minutes shrink as Edmonton keeps winning
